cells.tense: You are standing here without needing the next move solved first.
cells.ask: Pick one possibility sitting in you and do its smallest next step today. Not the whole plan, just the step that ends in the world instead of your head.
cells.core:
You are open right now in a way that is not uncertainty. Things can arrive and nothing has to be forced into a shape yet. That readiness is the whole point of this place, not a stage you are passing through.

Most people call this waiting. It is not waiting. It is the open hand before it closes on anything, and you notice it before you name it. From here something in you gets to come forward as itself, no performance, no practice run. Choose one small thing and let it be real; the rest stays yours to keep choosing.
cells.sheetLine: You are standing here with nothing decided, and that is the work.
cells.verb: Holding every possibility open before choosing one
cells.place: Where what you already are is allowed to show

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that will not let itself be written in yet.
cells.ask: Say one option out loud to a person who can hear it, then let it stand there unanswered. Do not explain or defend it today.
cells.core:
You keep every option open and call it freedom. That is how it feels from inside. What it costs is quieter: hours spent comparing roads you do not walk down.

Worked well, this holds a hinge — you keep the question alive and still close on something, then stay curious after the closing. Lately the closing keeps sliding past. The version ahead shifts because one thing is not being allowed to become true; somewhere you took on that choosing shuts things down, so nothing gets chosen, and nothing gets to show. The openness is real. Set one thing down and find out what is actually there.

cells.tense: Part of you is still standing at a door that shut, and it keeps standing there.
cells.ask: Name the whole pattern in what you have been doing this month, out loud or in writing, without scoring it as pass or fail.
cells.core:
Something in you stopped being open, and it happened before this week. Where the door was, you cannot point to it now — but the habit is visible: nothing new arrives without permission, and permission is not being issued.

What you make comes out narrow and careful, not because you cannot make, but because the entry is sealed. You can feel the constriction even while it works. Step back and look at the shape of your last month as if from outside; you can see it whole and still be inside it, and what you see keeps giving you something to use.

cells.tense: You are already steering this, and you talk about it as though it were moving on its own.
cells.ask: For one decision, describe what you would do if you believed you had options, then act on just that one thing today.
cells.core:
You move through this without catching yourself in the act of choosing. It is there; you answer what is in front of you so fast that the picking gets no look. What you are becoming is already underway, and you would say it is just how things went.

At its best, a person can feel the hand in the middle of it — a beat of noticing before the response, and the pick reads as theirs. Something else takes the credit. There is a smaller move you can reach today: the older way of imagining, from before you settled what was possible. Take one step only you could have chosen, and watch who gets the credit.
